'''Sergio de Larrea Asenjo''' (born 4 December 2005) is a Spanish [[basketball]] player for the [[Dallas Mavericks]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He previously played for [[Valencia Basket]]. In international competitions he represents the [[Spain men's national basketball team|Spanish national team]].

==Early life==
De Larrea was born on 4 December 2005 in [[Valladolid]], Spain.<ref name="auto2">{{Cite web|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/player/Sergio-De-Larrea/Summary/175825|publisher=[[RealGM]]|title=Sergio De Larrea}}</ref> His parents both played [[basketball]], with his father being a member of Club Deportivo Universitario and his mother playing for the team at the [[University of Valladolid]].<ref name="auto">{{Cite news|url=https://elpais.com/deportes/baloncesto/2024-12-15/sergio-de-larrea-el-espartano-que-ha-roto-el-molde.html|newspaper=[[El País]]|language=Spanish|title=Sergio de Larrea, el espartano que ha roto el molde|trans-title=Sergio de Larrea, the Spartan who has broken the mold|date=15 December 2024|author=Miñana, Fernando}}</ref> He grew up playing basketball and attended Colegio San Agustín.<ref name="auto1">{{Cite news|url=https://www.elnortedecastilla.es/deportes/baloncesto/ofertas-tentadoras-estados-unidos-debo-cegarme-dinero-20240910105645-nt.html|newspaper=[[El Norte de Castilla]]|language=Spanish|title=El vallisoletano Sergio de Larrea posa en la pista central de L'Alqueria. |trans-title=Valladolid native Sergio de Larrea poses on the center court at L'Alqueria.|author=Luis Bort, José|date=10 September 2024}}</ref> After playing for a time with the team at his school, he left to join the club [[Valencia Basket]], training with their youth team.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.diariodevalladolid.es/deportes/241225/266390/sergio-larrea-vallisoletano-cabeza-nba.html|newspaper=[[Diario de Valladolid]]|language=Spanish|title=Sergio de Larrea, un vallisoletano en la cabeza de la NBA|trans-title=Sergio de Larrea, a Valladolid native at the head of the NBA|author=Velasco, Guillermo|date=25 December 2024}}</ref>

==Professional career==

=== Valencia (2021–2026) ===
De Larrea averaged 8.0 points for the Valencia U18 team in the 2020–21 season, then averaged 18.0 points for the Valencia reserve team in the [[Segunda FEB|Segunda LEB]] (third-tier) in 2021–22.<ref name="auto2"/> He played most of the 2022–23 season with {{ill|CB L'Horta Godella|es}} in the LEB league, averaging 10.1 points.<ref name="auto2"/> He was promoted and made his senior debut for Valencia in January 2023, in [[EuroLeague]] play, at the age of 17.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.euroleaguebasketball.net/en/eurocup/news/top-10-eurocup-rising-star-award-candidates/|publisher=[[EuroLeague]]|title=Top 10 EuroCup Rising Star Award candidates|author=Sachs, Frankie|date=20 September 2024}}</ref> He returned to L'Horta Godella in 2023–24 and averaged 13.7 points, while also appearing in two games for Valencia.<ref name="auto2"/><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://as.com/baloncesto/mas_baloncesto/sergio-de-larrea-otra-joya-del-baloncesto-espanol-n/|newspaper=[[Diario AS]]|language=Spanish|title=Sergio de Larrea, otra joya del baloncesto español|trans-title=Sergio de Larrea, another gem of Spanish basketball|date=27 June 2024|author=Rubio, Juanma}}</ref> After declining offers to play [[college basketball]] in the U.S., he returned to Valencia for the 2024–25 season. He played regularly for the team at [[point guard]].<ref name="auto"/><ref name="auto1"/> Finishing the 2024-25 season, De Larrea played sparingly and averaged 3.6 points, 2.2 assists, and 2.2 rebounds.

Entering the 2025-26 season, De Larrea became a key player for Valencia and was playing a career-high number of minutes. During the 2025-26 season, De Larrea averaged 9.7 points, 3.7 assists, and 3 rebounds, making it a career high for De Larrea across his stats sheets. De Larrea also made it to the Spanish League championship, where Valencia defeated [[FC Barcelona Bàsquet|FC Barcelona]] 3-1.<ref>{{cite web
 |title=Valencia Wins the Spanish League Championship
|url=https://www.euroleaguebasketball.net/euroleague/news/valencia-wins-the-spanish-league-championship/
 |website=[[Euroleague Basketball]]
 |date=June 24, 2026
 |access-date=June 26, 2026
}}</ref><ref>{{cite web
 |title=Valencia secure second Spanish League title in club history
 |url=https://basketnews.com/news-250500-valencia-secure-second-spanish-league-title-in-club-history.html
 |website=[[BasketNews]]
 |date=June 24, 2026
 |access-date=June 26, 2026
}}</ref> During the series, he posted averages of 9.7 points, 3.7 assists, and 3.0 rebounds in just over 18 minutes per game.<ref>{{cite web

}}</ref>

=== Dallas Mavericks (2026–present) ===
On April 24, 2026, De Larrea declared for the [[2026 NBA Draft]].<ref name="BasketNewsDeLarrea2026">{{cite web |last=BasketNews.com Staff |title=Valencia guard declares for NBA Draft |url=https://basketnews.com/news-245906-sergio-de-larrea-declares-for-nba-draft.html |website=[[BasketNews]] |date=April 25, 2026 |access-date=July 9, 2026}}</ref> On June 23, 2026, De Larrea was selected with the 25th overall pick by the [[Los Angeles Lakers]], but his rights were subsequently traded to the [[New York Knicks]] for the draft rights to [[Cameron Carr (basketball)|Cameron Carr]]. Following the trade, De Larrea's draft rights were traded again, this time to the [[Dallas Mavericks]] in a three-team trade which saw [[Koa Peat]] go to the [[Phoenix Suns]], while the Knicks got three second-round picks and cash considerations.<ref>{{cite news |title=Mavs Acquire Draft Rights to 25th Overall Pick Sergio De Larrea|url=https://www.nba.com/mavs/news/mavs-acquire-draft-rights-to-25th-overall-pick-sergio-de-larrea|work=nba.com|date=June 24, 2026 |access-date=June 24, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=|first=|title=Who is Sergio De Larrea? 5 things to know about the draft prospect reportedly joining the Mavs |url=https://www.dallasnews.com/sports/mavericks/article/sergio-de-larrea-things-to-know-dallas-mavericks-22317223.php |work=[[The Dallas Morning News]] |date=June 24, 2026 |access-date=June 24, 2026}}</ref> After facing concerns of being drafted and stashed in the [[EuroLeague]], [[general manager]] [[Masai Ujiri]] and Mike Schmitz confirmed that De Larrea would be appearing on the [[2026–27 Dallas Mavericks season]].<ref>{{cite web
 |title=Mavericks GM addresses Sergio De Larrea's status for 2026-27 season
|url=https://therookiewire.usatoday.com/story/sports/nba/rookie/2026/06/25/mavericks-sergio-de-larrea-valencia-nba-contract/90697316007/
 |website=Rookie Wire
 |publisher=[[USA Today]]
 |date=June 25, 2026
 |access-date=June 26, 2026
}}</ref> On July 3, 2026, De Larrea signed a standard contract with the Mavericks and he will be participating with the team during the [[2026 NBA Summer League]].<ref name="DMN_DeLarrea">{{cite web |last=Curtis |first=Mike |url=https://www.dallasnews.com/sports/mavericks/article/mavericks-sign-sergio-de-larrea-22331907.php |title=Mavericks sign Sergio de Larrea |website=[[The Dallas Morning News]]|date=July 3, 2026 |access-date=July 3, 2026}}</ref> In his 2026 NBA Summer League series with the Mavericks, De Larrea averaged 8 points, 4.8 rebounds, and 8.8 assists throughout four games.<ref name="realgmmavssummerleague">{{cite web|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/nba/teams/Dallas-Mavericks/6/Rosters/Summer_League|title=2026 Dallas 2026 NBA Summer League Stats|website=[[RealGM]] |date=July 17, 2026 |access-date=July 18, 2026}}</ref>

==International career==
De Larrea helped Spain win a silver medal at the [[2022 FIBA Under-17 Basketball World Cup]].<ref name="auto3">{{Cite news|url=https://www.marca.com/baloncesto/seleccion/2024/06/28/667f075022601da95a8b45ff.html|newspaper=[[Marca (newspaper)|Marca]]|language=Spanish|title=Sergio De Larrea, la última perla del baloncesto español, causa sensación|trans-title=Sergio De Larrea, the latest gem of Spanish basketball, causes a sensation|author=Luis Martínez, José|date=28 June 2024}}</ref> The following year, he helped Spain win the [[2023 FIBA Under-19 Basketball World Cup]], and in 2024, he competed at the [[2024 FIBA U20 EuroBasket|European U20 championship]].<ref name="auto3"/> He was called up to the [[Spain men's national basketball team|senior national team]] and trained with them prior to the [[2024 Summer Olympics]].<ref name="auto4">{{Cite web|url=https://www.valenciabasket.com/?p=noticias&noticia=10994&lang=en|publisher=[[Valencia Basket]]|title=Sergio De Larrea joins the Valencia Basket first men's team |date=5 July 2024}}</ref> He made his senior national debut against the [[Dominican Republic men's national basketball team|Dominican Republic]] in June 2024.<ref name="auto4"/>
